newsitem.title: USA: No agreement on NATO reached in U.S. talks-Millon.
newsitem.headline: No agreement on NATO reached in U.S. talks-Millon.

text.p: The United States and France reached no agreement on the dispute over U.S. command of NATO forces in southern Europe in talks this week, French Defence Minister Charles Millon said on Tuesday.

Speaking to reporters after talks with U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen, Millon said: "I cannot say we reached agreement today," but he added, "I'm confident that one of these days we will find something in common."

Millon said the talks with Cohen centred on the post-Cold War adaptation of NATO, including reform of NATO's Southern Command headquarters in Naples, Italy. France wants this post be turned over by Washington to a European officer.
France has tied the issue to its decision on whether to join the military wing of a reformed NATO alliance.
"We want to reach a new military balance between the United States and Europe," Millon said through a translator. "We want to reach actual parity in the southern region."

"What France wants to see is a balanced evolution of the structures of NATO ... What France requests today is basically to actually share responsibilities on an equal footing," Millon said. "In terms of Europe, responsibility for Europeans in the framework of NATO, these responsibilities have to be taken over by Europeans."

At the Pentagon earlier, Millon made no comment on an Italian compromise proposal that a decision be deferred for at least five years but said "obviously in order to have a reinforced Atlantic alliance we need to have parity in this area."
In Rome on March 7, Cohen called the Italian compromise "a very constructive proposal."

Regarding NATO expansion into central Europe, Millon stressed France's position that Romania should be considered a candidate for membership in the "first wave" of expansion that now is expected to include Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
